summary: John's 8th-great-grandfather; Philipstown (Hudson Highlands) pioneer, called 'Captain', commissioner of highways for Dutchess County.
bio: Thomas Davenport was born in 1682 (Davenport family Bible) and died in 1759; his will was dated 1746 and proved 1760. He was a pioneer of Philipstown in the Hudson Highlands, commissioner of highways for Dutchess County 1745-49, and called 'Captain'. In 1752 he deeded Goshen-precinct land to his daughter 'Charity Lamoree, wife of John Lamoree'. Westchester deeds show William Davenport senior of the Manor of Fordham 'conveyed to my son Thomas Davenport' land, and a 1718 deed names William Jr. and Thomas as 'sons of William Davenport' (probable father). His second wife Elizabeth was 'believed' to be a Leggett sister (WikiTree's chain Leggett -> Richardson -> Mead of Watford rests on that belief; speculative). Family descent from Rev. John Davenport of New Haven is disproven ('the last, we know, to be untrue', Giles & Franklin p.xix), and the Davenport of Bromhall/Bramhall, Cheshire link is unsupported. Possible Society of Colonial Wars qualifying ancestor.
